name: Imagen AI
tagline: Apply reusable local adjustment presets and keep every edit reversible

pricing.notes: Pricing is usage based per photo; canonical monthly amount is null.

tiers.name: Pay-as-you-go
tiers.limits: No edit-volume cap; 2 computers; base color editing starts at $0.05 per photo.
tiers.notes: The $7 monthly minimum becomes editing credit and rolls over; there is no annual PAYG option for new self-serve subscribers.

tiers.name: Limitless
tiers.limits: Unlimited editing, retouching, AI tools and AI culling for 1 individual photographer; 2 computers.
tiers.notes: Published annual rate is $179/month billed upfront for the year; a monthly option exists, but its current USD price did not render.

tiers.name: Business
tiers.limits: Multiple photographers/computers, API access and high-volume capacity; 0 self-serve prices published.

pricing.freeTierCaps: no free tier; 1,000-edit free trial with no credit card
pricing.billingTerms: PAYG monthly; Limitless monthly or annual prepaid (annual saves about 20%); Business custom
pricing.hiddenCosts: On PAYG, straighten/crop/portrait crop/headshot crop/smooth skin/subject mask are $0.20 per photo each; culling starts at $29/month and cloud backup starts at $29/month. PAYG credits are non-refundable; Limitless excludes teams and the separate Imagen for Real Estate product.

verdictSummary: A consolation build is possible, but the paid product's decisive value sits outside a solo rebuild. For Imagen AI, apply reusable local adjustment presets and keep every edit reversible. The hard boundary is proprietary photographer-trained models, cloud processing, profiles, and workflow integration, plus image pipeline quality, models, and workflow polish.
coreLoopDIY: Catalog local photos, generate previews, apply reusable non-destructive adjustment presets, keep every edit reversible, and export selected originals or rendered copies.
whatYouLose: proprietary photographer-trained models, cloud processing, profiles, and workflow integration
moatNotes: image pipeline quality, models, and workflow polish
ongoingBurden: raw codecs, color management, metadata, previews, face models, GPU support, storage, backups, sync, and export fidelity
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Imagen AI because photographers pay because image quality, catalog safety, and fast handling of huge libraries matter more than cloning sliders. The recurring cost buys raw codecs, color management, metadata, previews, face models, GPU support, storage, backups, sync, and export fidelity, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Immich
priorArt.desc: Active open-source self-hosted photo and video management platform.

alternatives.name: darktable
alternatives.desc: Reusable styles, presets, history, sidecars, and fully reversible local adjustments; it learns nothing about your taste, which is both flaw and feature.

facts.install: Install the Windows executable, macOS disk image, Linux package, Flatpak, or AppImage
facts.engines: A local non-generative imaging pipeline; current releases can use ONNX models for subject masking, denoising, and image upscaling without a cloud account
facts.dataFormat: Original photos stay untouched; edits, ratings, tags, and history are stored in a local SQLite library and portable XMP sidecar files, with thumbnails and cache data in the user profile
facts.gapVsPaid: Styles and presets are deterministic rather than learned from the photographer's prior edits, so they cannot adapt each image in the personalized way Imagen does.
facts.setupBlocker: macOS may require a Gatekeeper right-click Open or xattr step; the larger obstacle is learning darktable's module-heavy workflow rather than installation

alternatives.name: RapidRAW
alternatives.desc: Non-destructive presets, masks, batch edits, and local processing in a modern app; no personalized AI style model, no recurring bill.

facts.install: Install the Windows .exe, macOS .dmg, or Linux AppImage/DEB/Flatpak; Android is an experimental sideload
facts.engines: Local subject, sky, and foreground masking, NIND denoising, LaMa inpainting, and optional handoff to a user-run ComfyUI backend
facts.dataFormat: Photos are never moved; non-destructive adjustments are stored in a documented .rrdata sidecar next to each image, while thumbnails, logs, and downloaded models live in local application data
facts.gapVsPaid: Its presets and masks stay reversible, but it does not train a personal editing profile or adapt batch decisions to each photograph.
facts.setupBlocker: Desktop binaries are unsigned, so Windows SmartScreen and macOS Gatekeeper need manual bypass steps; Linux AppImage users may also need libfuse2

alternatives.name: RawTherapee
alternatives.desc: Processing profiles and sidecars make repeatable RAW adjustments completely reversible; automation is deterministic, not psychic.

facts.install: Install the Windows installer, macOS disk image, or Linux AppImage/distribution package
facts.dataFormat: Original RAW files remain unchanged; processing settings are saved as human-readable .pp3 sidecars beside the image or in the local cache, and rendered exports go to a chosen folder
facts.gapVsPaid: Processing profiles repeat exact settings, but they do not learn taste or make image-specific personalized adjustments the way Imagen does.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Immich
rejectedAlternatives.desc: It preserves originals and metadata, but it is a photo backup system, not a reversible preset-and-adjustment engine.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Pay as you go plan and a personal local photo catalog DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a closest honest personal substitute for Imagen AI in an empty repository.
Use Tauri 2, React, TypeScript, Rust image libraries, SQLite, and local filesystem access; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: catalog local photos, generate previews, apply reusable non-destructive adjustment presets, keep every edit reversible, and export selected originals or rendered copies.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Index selected folders without moving or rewriting originals and store only catalog data in SQLite.
Generate thumbnails and previews, read EXIF, detect duplicates by hash, and monitor file changes.
Provide timeline, folders, albums, ratings, flags, tags, search, and side-by-side compare.
Store edits as reversible parameters for crop, rotate, exposure, contrast, white balance, and saturation.
Render exports to a new folder with explicit color space, quality, size, and metadata choices.
Add catalog backup, missing-file repair, integrity scan, and a clear original-safety guarantee.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Do not claim to reproduce proprietary data, network liquidity, regulated access, or frontier infrastructure.
Deliberately leave out a proprietary raw-rendering engine.
Deliberately leave out hosted cross-device photo sync and client galleries.
Deliberately leave out frontier culling, retouching, and generative models.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
